# Evaluation Report

**Latest run:** 2026-11-17; 30 deterministic scenarios. Machine-readable details are in [`evaluation-results.json`](evaluation-results.json), generated by `python -m backend.evaluation.run_eval`.

| Measure | Result |
|---|---:|
| Outcome accuracy | 29/30 = 0.9667 |
| Classification accuracy | 21/28 = 0.7500 |
| Escalation correctness | 1.0000 |
| Clarification correctness | 1.0000 |
| Retrieval precision@k / recall@k | 0.0000 / 0.0000 on labeled primary-law passages |
| Mean lexical context relevance | 0.1391 |
| Safe abstention rate | 1.0000 |
| Answer-run denominator | 0 |
| Mean / max scenario latency | 22.37 / 55.96 ms |

This suite exercises deterministic guardrails, routing, and corpus retrieval. It does not generate or judge legal answers. Citation correctness/completeness, groundedness, faithfulness, unsupported-claim rate, and hallucination rate are therefore null/not measured, not zero.

Scenario G05 expects an answer to the 18-month fixed-term gratuity question. Its actual outcome is `LEGAL_COUNSEL_REVIEW`, because the Code on Social Security section 53 text is not locally indexed. That mismatch is intentional evidence of an unresolved legal-source blocker; do not change the oracle or verifier to force a pass.

The historical 20-case run is superseded. The latest evaluation details include classification outcomes separately from decision accuracy. Retrieval relevance is lexical token overlap and is not a measure of legal correctness.
